tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 2) | cite: ASME Y14.41-2019 Annex B; ISO 10303-242 cl8.3.2

tips.title: Recognize pocket faces BEFORE fillet/round edges
tips.body: Recognize pocket faces BEFORE fillet/round edges | formula/threshold: tag const-radius adjacent if r<0.25*depth
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 2) | cite: ISO 10303-42 cl4.5.1 p.52; Zeid p.352

tips.title: Thread-mill cutter dia must sit well below thread minor dia; helical-interpolation profile (arc vs true flank) error grows with D_c/D_thread
tips.body: Thread-mill cutter dia must sit well below thread minor dia; helical-interpolation profile (arc vs true flank) error grows with D_c/D_thread | formula/threshold: D_c <= 0.7 x D_thread (0.6 x for close tol); must clear minor dia
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: Sandvik Coromant threading guide + field-practice

tips.title: Thin-wall: rough both faces leaving equal thin stock, finish top-down in a staircase with light spring passes, keep support material on the
tips.body: Thin-wall: rough both faces leaving equal thin stock, finish top-down in a staircase with light spring passes, keep support material on the opposite side until last | formula/threshold: ~0.1-0.2 mm finish stock/wall; alternate sides; light final
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: field-practice (uncited)

tips.title: High-feed milling (distinct from chip-thinning): small lead/entry angle steers force axially into the stiffest spindle direction at shallow
tips.body: High-feed milling (distinct from chip-thinning): small lead/entry angle steers force axially into the stiffest spindle direction at shallow axial DOC + high feed/tooth | formula/threshold: lead angle ~10-17 deg; a_p ~0.5-2 mm; force axial (+Z)
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: Sandvik / Ingersoll high-feed guides + field-practice

tips.title: Micro-tool runout: TIR must be <= ~3% of dia or one flute carries the whole load and snaps; measure at the cutting edge, not the shank
tips.body: Micro-tool runout: TIR must be <= ~3% of dia or one flute carries the whole load and snaps; measure at the cutting edge, not the shank | formula/threshold: TIR <= 0.03 x D_c (~3 um for D < 1 mm)
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: field-practice (uncited)

tips.title: Internal-corner feed reduction holds the contact-point (edge) velocity constant as the tool-center slows through the corner
tips.body: Internal-corner feed reduction holds the contact-point (edge) velocity constant as the tool-center slows through the corner | formula/threshold: f_center = f_prog x (R_i - R_tool)/R_i; floor 30-50% when R_i ~ 1.1-1.3 x R_tool
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: field-practice (uncited)

tips.title: Stainless/nickel face-mill: positive roll-in (arc) entry, NEVER dwell/rub (ISO-M/S work-harden under a rubbing edge); a large lead thins the
tips.body: Stainless/nickel face-mill: positive roll-in (arc) entry, NEVER dwell/rub (ISO-M/S work-harden under a rubbing edge); a large lead thins the chip but is a productivity choice, not the anti-work-harden lever | formula/threshold: arc roll-in entry; no dwell; fz above rubbing floor
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: Sandvik milling guide + field-practice

tips.title: Cutter-to-slot-width: avoid a cutter near the slot width (0.6-0.8 x re-cuts chips on the trailing edge) and avoid full-slot a_e = D (180 deg
tips.body: Cutter-to-slot-width: avoid a cutter near the slot width (0.6-0.8 x re-cuts chips on the trailing edge) and avoid full-slot a_e = D (180 deg wrap) -- prefer peel/trochoidal | formula/threshold: prefer D <= 0.7 x slot width + trochoidal
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: Sandvik pocketing guidance + field-practice

tips.title: Climb (down) milling by default on rigid CNC (chip thick->thin: less edge heat, better finish); conventional only for hard skin/scale or bac
tips.body: Climb (down) milling by default on rigid CNC (chip thick->thin: less edge heat, better finish); conventional only for hard skin/scale or backlash-prone machines | formula/threshold: default climb
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: Machinery's Handbook (climb vs conventional) + Sandvik

tips.title: Tailstock quill extension limit -- quill deflection scales ~ extension^3 (cantilever); keep minimal, retract before high RPM
tips.body: Tailstock quill extension limit -- quill deflection scales ~ extension^3 (cantilever); keep minimal, retract before high RPM | formula/threshold: quill extension <= 3 x quill diameter
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: Machinery's Handbook (tailstock rigidity) + field-practice

tips.title: Thread run-out/chamfer is set by the Fanuc G76 chamfer parameter (not a helix-angle formula); size the relief groove so the synchronized ret
tips.body: Thread run-out/chamfer is set by the Fanuc G76 chamfer parameter (not a helix-angle formula); size the relief groove so the synchronized retract clears the shoulder before spindle-lead desync | formula/threshold: G76 chamfer field (0.1L increments, 0-89 deg)
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: Fanuc Series 0i/0i-TF Operator's Manual, G76 threading cycle

tips.title: Live-tool / C-axis rigid tapping needs exact spindle-to-feed sync: axial feed per rev must equal the thread pitch; without rigid-tap sync us
tips.body: Live-tool / C-axis rigid tapping needs exact spindle-to-feed sync: axial feed per rev must equal the thread pitch; without rigid-tap sync use a tension-compression (floating) tap holder | formula/threshold: F[mm/min] = pitch[mm/rev] x S[rpm] (feed/rev = pitch)
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: Fanuc rigid-tapping (G84/G74) function

tips.title: Minimum bar remnant must keep full collet/pusher grip + spindle-liner engagement -- a short remnant lets the pusher feed air and crash the t
tips.body: Minimum bar remnant must keep full collet/pusher grip + spindle-liner engagement -- a short remnant lets the pusher feed air and crash the turret | formula/threshold: remnant >= collet grip length + pad; verify per bar-feeder OEM
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: field-practice (uncited)

tips.title: Hard-turn white-layer is THERMAL, not a fixed Vc/VB line: forms when surface temp reaches austenitization onset; rising Vc + flank wear both
tips.body: Hard-turn white-layer is THERMAL, not a fixed Vc/VB line: forms when surface temp reaches austenitization onset; rising Vc + flank wear both raise that temp, so worn insert + high Vc are the trigger | formula/threshold: threshold_C: hardened 700 / steel 850 / stainless 650
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: mcp-server/src/physics/constants.ts WHITE_LAYER_THRESHOLDS (Klocke; Boothroyd 1963)

tips.title: Boring/ID-groove bar deflection must consume only a fraction of the print tolerance band, especially at overhang L/D > 4 where deflection ~
tips.body: Boring/ID-groove bar deflection must consume only a fraction of the print tolerance band, especially at overhang L/D > 4 where deflection ~ (L/D)^3 dominates diameter error | formula/threshold: budget delta_radial <= ~0.5 x tolerance band
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: field-practice + Machinery's Handbook cantilever delta = FL^3/3EI

tips.title: Deionized-water dielectric resistivity is in the MEGOHM-cm range (NOT kOhm-cm); finishing wants HIGH resistivity, roughing runs LOWER; below
tips.body: Deionized-water dielectric resistivity is in the MEGOHM-cm range (NOT kOhm-cm); finishing wants HIGH resistivity, roughing runs LOWER; below ~3 MOhm.cm discharges go unstable + the deionizer resin is spent | formula/threshold: finishing ~5-15 MOhm.cm; regen resin < ~3 MOhm.cm. (a draft "50-150 kOhm.cm" is ~100x too conductive)
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: PRISM tribal wedm-kb-007 + Jameson, EDM (SME 2001) dielectric-conditioning

tips.title: Thin walls / small unsupported sections: REDUCE flush pressure -- a high jet vibrates the wire and deflects the wall (straightness + Ra loss
tips.body: Thin walls / small unsupported sections: REDUCE flush pressure -- a high jet vibrates the wire and deflects the wall (straightness + Ra loss); aggressive flushing is a roughing/deep-cut tool | formula/threshold: skim/thin-section ~3-5 bar vs 8-10 bar roughing
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: PRISM tribal wedm-kb (reduce flush on skim) + field-practice

tips.title: Wire-guide wear/contamination raises effective wire tension and causes fatigue breaks BEFORE it shows as size error; replace on a running-ho
tips.body: Wire-guide wear/contamination raises effective wire tension and causes fatigue breaks BEFORE it shows as size error; replace on a running-hours cadence keyed to material abrasiveness | formula/threshold: replace guides ~200-400 h (material-dependent); flag tension variation > ~15%
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: PRISM tribal wedm-kb-006 + Sommer, Complete EDM Handbook (guide maintenance)

tips.title: Wire TRAVEL speed is a break-risk / wire-presentation control, NOT a recast control -- recast/HAZ depth is set by discharge ENERGY (pulse-on
tips.body: Wire TRAVEL speed is a break-risk / wire-presentation control, NOT a recast control -- recast/HAZ depth is set by discharge ENERGY (pulse-on, peak current), so cut recast with low-energy skim passes, not by tuning m/min | formula/threshold: recast ~ per-spark energy (V x I x t_on), not wire m/min
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: field-practice + Jameson, EDM (SME 2001)

tips.title: On a wire break, cap auto-rethread retries and let the dielectric stabilize before restart -- blind repeated re-thread into a debris-fouled
tips.body: On a wire break, cap auto-rethread retries and let the dielectric stabilize before restart -- blind repeated re-thread into a debris-fouled kerf wastes wire and can bird-nest | formula/threshold: ~2-3 auto-rethread attempts then operator halt
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: field-practice (uncited)

tips.title: Dielectric fire / water-level interlock: the workpiece must stay submerged during sparking -- exposed sparking above the waterline can ignit
tips.body: Dielectric fire / water-level interlock: the workpiece must stay submerged during sparking -- exposed sparking above the waterline can ignite oil residue/additives or pocket explosive hydrogen; a dropping tank level must auto-pause the cut | formula/threshold: maintain > ~25 mm dielectric coverage above the part; tank-level sensor auto-pause
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: PRISM tribal wedm-kb (safety) + OSHA/NFPA EDM fire-safety guidance

tips.title: Start (thread) hole must sit off the contour with a straight lead-in and be clearly larger than the wire+guide geometry -- a hole only margi
tips.body: Start (thread) hole must sit off the contour with a straight lead-in and be clearly larger than the wire+guide geometry -- a hole only marginally over wire dia defeats auto-thread after a break, especially inside a tight radius | formula/threshold: ~2-3 mm off contour, straight lead-in; hole >> wire dia (a ~0.3 mm-over hole is too tight)
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: PRISM tribal wedm-kb-020 + Guitrau, The EDM Handbook

tips.title: Pencil/rest-machining tool reachability: the tool radius must be strictly smaller than the smallest concave (internal fillet) radius it must
tips.body: Pencil/rest-machining tool reachability: the tool radius must be strictly smaller than the smallest concave (internal fillet) radius it must reach, else the pass leaves uncut stock | formula/threshold: r_tool < smallest concave fillet radius on the surface
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: field-practice (uncited)

tips.title: Ball-nose concave-surface gouge guard on finish/flowline passes: the ball radius must be <= the smallest concave surface-curvature radius (a
tips.body: Ball-nose concave-surface gouge guard on finish/flowline passes: the ball radius must be <= the smallest concave surface-curvature radius (a larger ball gouges tight concave regions) | formula/threshold: r_ball <= R_min (smallest concave curvature radius)
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: field-practice (uncited)

tips.title: Prefer helical/ramp entry over vertical plunge into closed pockets -- avoids axial overload of non-center-cutting end mills and poor chip cl
tips.body: Prefer helical/ramp entry over vertical plunge into closed pockets -- avoids axial overload of non-center-cutting end mills and poor chip clearance at the pocket floor | formula/threshold: ramp/helix angle ~2-5 deg (shallower for hard/thin-web; steeper acceptable in open slots)
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: field-practice (uncited)

tips.title: Safe rapid (G0) linking / retract clearance plane above the highest stock + fixture obstacle; use stay-down linking below clearance ONLY whe
tips.body: Safe rapid (G0) linking / retract clearance plane above the highest stock + fixture obstacle; use stay-down linking below clearance ONLY when the connecting move is verified obstacle-free, else full retract | formula/threshold: clearance plane above highest obstacle + margin
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: field-practice (uncited)

tips.title: Rotary-axis wind-up: insert an unwind/rewind before accumulated commanded rotary angle reaches the axis rotary travel limit (protects a cabl
tips.body: Rotary-axis wind-up: insert an unwind/rewind before accumulated commanded rotary angle reaches the axis rotary travel limit (protects a cable-carrier axis) -- the limit is machine-specific, NOT a universal 720 deg | formula/threshold: unwind before | NOTE: citation is LLM-asserted, not page-verified -- confirm the source before relying on it
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: accumulated C/A

tips.title: Internal (concave) arc tool-center feed compensation to hold the tool-tip/surface feed constant: factor R/(R - r_tool); external/convex arc
tips.body: Internal (concave) arc tool-center feed compensation to hold the tool-tip/surface feed constant: factor R/(R - r_tool); external/convex arc factor R/(R + r_tool) < 1. (a draft "1 - arc_r/tool_dia" is wrong-direction) | formula/threshold: f_center factor = R/(R - r_tool) internal; R/(R + r_tool) external
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: Smid, CNC Programming Handbook (arc feedrate compensation under cutter comp)

tips.title: Polar-coordinate interpolation differs by control -- Fanuc mill G16 (on)/G15 (cancel); lathe/mill-turn C-axis face/OD is G12.1 (on)/G13.1 (o
tips.body: Polar-coordinate interpolation differs by control -- Fanuc mill G16 (on)/G15 (cancel); lathe/mill-turn C-axis face/OD is G12.1 (on)/G13.1 (off); Siemens TRANSMIT/TRACYL (cancel TRAFOOF, NOT a G-code); Heidenhain CC (pole)+LP/CP. TRAP: G16 != G12.1 -- never emit G16 on a mill-turn face-C job | formula/threshold: Fanuc G16/G15 vs G12.1/G13.1 vs Siemens TRANSMIT/TRACYL
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: Smid, CNC Programming Handbook 3e + Siemens 840D sl Cycles/Transformations

tips.title: Mirror/scale differ by control -- Fanuc G51.1/G50.1 (scale G51/G50); Siemens MIRROR/AMIRROR + SCALE/ASCALE; Heidenhain CYCL DEF 8 (mirror)/1
tips.body: Mirror/scale differ by control -- Fanuc G51.1/G50.1 (scale G51/G50); Siemens MIRROR/AMIRROR + SCALE/ASCALE; Heidenhain CYCL DEF 8 (mirror)/11 (scale); Haas mirror = Settings 45-48 (NOT a G-code -- "G101" is wrong) | formula/threshold: Fanuc G51.1/G50.1 vs Siemens MIRROR vs Haas Settings 45-48
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: Fanuc 30i/31i Operator's Manual B-64484EN + Heidenhain iTNC 530 Cycle 8/11

tips.title: 5-axis TCP (tool center point) differs by control -- Fanuc G43.4/G49; Haas G234/G49; Siemens TRAORI/TRAFOOF; Heidenhain M128/M129; Okuma OSP
tips.body: 5-axis TCP (tool center point) differs by control -- Fanuc G43.4/G49; Haas G234/G49; Siemens TRAORI/TRAFOOF; Heidenhain M128/M129; Okuma OSP G169 (on)/G170 (off, NOT G168). Non-cancel of TCP = crash on the next positioning move | formula/threshold: Fanuc G43.4 . Haas G234 . Siemens TRAORI . Heidenhain M128 . Okuma G169/G170
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: Haas Mill Manual (G234 TCPC) + Fanuc B-64484EN + Okuma OSP 5-axis (verified vs JM .cps)

tips.title: 3+2 indexed tilted-plane is DISTINCT from simultaneous TCP -- Fanuc G68.2 (Euler)+G53.1/G69; Siemens CYCLE800; Heidenhain PLANE SPATIAL/RESE
tips.body: 3+2 indexed tilted-plane is DISTINCT from simultaneous TCP -- Fanuc G68.2 (Euler)+G53.1/G69; Siemens CYCLE800; Heidenhain PLANE SPATIAL/RESET; Haas G268/G269. TRAP: G68.2 (5-axis WCS tilt) != G54.4 (workpiece-error comp) != G68 (2D rotation) | formula/threshold: Fanuc G68.2+G53.1 vs Siemens CYCLE800 vs Haas G268
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: Fanuc 30i B-64484EN (Tilted Working Plane) + Siemens 840D sl CYCLE800

tips.title: Probing macro + result storage differ -- Renishaw Inspection Plus G65 P9810 is PROTECTED-POSITIONING (a guarded rapid, NOT a measure); measu
tips.body: Probing macro + result storage differ -- Renishaw Inspection Plus G65 P9810 is PROTECTED-POSITIONING (a guarded rapid, NOT a measure); measure macros are P9811 (surface)/P9814 (bore-boss)/P9815; results land in commons #100-#144 (#138 position, #144 size dev); Haas tool-set G65 P9023. Wrong P-number = probe crashes at rapid | formula/threshold: Fanuc/Haas/Okuma G65 P98xx (Renishaw); Siemens CYCLE977/978/982; Heidenhain TCH PROBE 4xx
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: Renishaw Inspection Plus Programming Manual H-2000-6222

tips.title: Feed-per-rev vs feed-per-min + encoder dependency -- G95 (per rev) REQUIRES a spindle encoder; G94 (per min) does not; lathe G95 is the turn
tips.body: Feed-per-rev vs feed-per-min + encoder dependency -- G95 (per rev) REQUIRES a spindle encoder; G94 (per min) does not; lathe G95 is the turning default, mill G95 is valid ONLY with a synchronized spindle (live-tool/threadmill/tap). Wrong mode = ~100x crawl (G95 num read as G94) or gross overfeed/crash (reverse) | formula/threshold: G95 (ipr, needs encoder) vs G94 (ipm)
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: Smid, CNC Programming Handbook (Feedrate Function) + Okuma OSP-P300L

tips.title: A thread designated as a datum feature establishes its axis from the PITCH cylinder by default; MAJOR DIA or MINOR DIA must be stated explic
tips.body: A thread designated as a datum feature establishes its axis from the PITCH cylinder by default; MAJOR DIA or MINOR DIA must be stated explicitly to override | formula/threshold: ASME Y14.5-2018 Sec 4 (screw threads/gears/splines as datum features)
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: ASME Y14.5-2018

tips.title: Tangent-plane modifier (circle-T) makes the tolerance zone control the contacting (tangent) high-point plane, not the surface -- local peaks
tips.body: Tangent-plane modifier (circle-T) makes the tolerance zone control the contacting (tangent) high-point plane, not the surface -- local peaks may lie outside the zone if the tangent plane conforms | formula/threshold: ASME Y14.5-2018 Sec 6 Orientation (modifier defined Sec 3 Symbology)
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: ASME Y14.5-2018

tips.title: Free-state modifier (circle-F) applies a tolerance to a non-rigid part in its unrestrained state; unless invoked, non-rigid parts are inspec
tips.body: Free-state modifier (circle-F) applies a tolerance to a non-rigid part in its unrestrained state; unless invoked, non-rigid parts are inspected RESTRAINED per an explicit restraint note on the drawing | formula/threshold: ASME Y14.5-2018 Sec 5 (Non-Rigid Parts / free state), restraint note
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: ASME Y14.5-2018

tips.title: ISO surface-texture lay symbol (=, perp, X, M, C, R, P) sets the dominant machining-pattern (lay) direction relative to the view projection
tips.body: ISO surface-texture lay symbol (=, perp, X, M, C, R, P) sets the dominant machining-pattern (lay) direction relative to the view projection plane -- orientation-carrying, not amplitude | formula/threshold: ISO 1302 lay-direction symbols (ASME Y14.36 equivalent)
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: ISO 1302

tips.title: Total runout is a composite surface control (form+orientation+location) -- full-indicator-movement over the ENTIRE surface (all circular + l
tips.body: Total runout is a composite surface control (form+orientation+location) -- full-indicator-movement over the ENTIRE surface (all circular + longitudinal elements); circular runout is per-cross-section only | formula/threshold: ASME Y14.5-2018 Sec 9 Runout (total vs circular)
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: ASME Y14.5-2018

tips.title: Runout referenced to a single cylindrical datum feature too short to stabilize the axis should reference TWO coaxial datum features as one d
tips.body: Runout referenced to a single cylindrical datum feature too short to stabilize the axis should reference TWO coaxial datum features as one datum axis (A-B) to constrain wobble | formula/threshold: ASME Y14.5-2018 Sec 9 Runout with co-datum axis
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: ASME Y14.5-2018

tips.title: STEP AP242 geometric validation properties (solid volume, surface area, centroid) are round-trip checksums written into the file so a transl
tips.body: STEP AP242 geometric validation properties (solid volume, surface area, centroid) are round-trip checksums written into the file so a translator/receiver can verify translated geometry matches the source -- compared by software, not a machine gate | formula/threshold: STEP geometric_validation_property (CAx-IF recommended practice; ISO 10303-242 with -59 data-quality principles)
tips.source: hermes:parallel-agent (wave 3) | cite: ISO 10303-242 / CAx-IF Validation Properties recommended practice
